en: The Lotus Sutra, Chapter Twenty-Nine: Measuring Heaven and Earth.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, wearing [his] robes...
Baring his right shoulder and placing his head upon the ground,
he paid homage to the Buddha, knelt with palms joined, and addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, we immeasurable multitudes of bodhisattvas, together with all the devas and humans, [are here]."
Having heard the various dharmas extensively before the Buddha and having expounded and explained the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*,
his mind was purified and filled with such unprecedented joy that he addressed the Buddha once more, saying:
“World-Honored One, I constantly travel back and forth throughout all the infinite worlds of the ten directions day and night to transform sentient beings;
yet I do not know the depth or shallowness, nor the proximity or distance, of heaven and earth.”
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain this for me, so that my great assembly may all hear it.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara and the bodhisattvas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River:
Listen attentively now and pay close heed;
I shall analyze and explain it for you.
Such as this is the great earth, twenty billion *li* in depth.
Next, there is a layer of moisture, also twenty billion *li* deep.
Next, there are various exquisite treasures—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, musaragalva, agate, coral, and amber—forty billion *li* deep.
Next is the layer of gold dust, eighty billion *yojana* deep;
next is the layer of silver and diamond, also eighty billion *yojana* deep;
next is the layer of silver dust, one hundred billion *yojana* deep.
Next, there is a layer of diamond [vajra] two hundred billion *li* deep.
Beneath it lies an infinite great wind that supports the heavens and earth, preventing them from tilting or shaking.
This great earth is the beam and pillar of heaven.
Why is this? Because all things that exist in the world depend upon the earth.
Furthermore, rivers, great oceans, small seas, surging waves, wells, valleys, grasses, trees, groves, medicinal herbs, and various plants all grow from the earth.
Mount Mālu, Mount Śaila, Mount Kṣudra-cakravāḍa, Mount Meru, Mount Vajra, Mount Sumeru, and so forth—
all such mountains of exquisite jewels, the kings among all mountains.
The four jewels surge forth and rise higher than all other mountains of exquisite jewels;
they are all formed by the emergence of precious gems from the great earth.
Furthermore, Sumeru, the king of mountains, is formed by the surging of the four jewels and rises above all worlds.
What are the four?
The south is named Vaidūrya;
the west is named Sphaṭika.
The north is named agate;
the east is named gold.
The radiant flames of these four jewels illuminate the four directions.
All sentient beings in the world gaze upon him together and call him "Heaven.
Mount Sumeru is where the World-Protecting Lords of Heaven (Lokapālas) dwell as their place of reliance.
To the south of Mount Sumeru, there are immeasurable palaces made of the seven treasures.
A hundred thousand *li* from the earth,
there is a celestial king named Vi within it.
